result.effect: High familiarity: 5.2% in 2023 vs 60% in 2025; active use: 36.8% in 2023 vs 91.7% in 2025

cells.quote:
In 2023, only5.2%ofrespondents reported high familiarity, while the majority fell into the medium category (68.4%) and over a quarter reported low familiarity (26.3%). By 2025, all respondents reported at least medium familiarity, and 60% reported high familiarity, suggesting that GenAI had become a more common and better understood tool before entering the course.
In 2023, only 36.8% reported active use, and a substantial portion reported no use. By 2025, GenAI use became nearly universal: 91.7% reported active use and only 8.3% reported no use.

result.effect: Kruskal–Wallis H=31.91, p<0.0001; means 3.05 in 2023, 4.68 in 2024, and 4.75 in 2025

cells.quote: Overall, requests increased substantially after 2023: the mean requests per student–week rose from 3.05 in 2023 to 4.68 in 2024 and remained comparable in 2025 (4.75). This cohort difference was statistically significant (Kruskal–WallisH= 31.91,p <0.0001), driven by the gap between 2023 and both later cohorts; the 2024 and 2025 cohorts did not differ significantly.

O.outcome_detail: Density and interconnectedness of prompt-type transition networks

cells.quote: The 2023 network is comparatively sparse with fewer strong transitions, suggesting shorter and less iterative interaction episodes. In 2024, the network becomes substantially more connected and exhibits a prominent verification-centered structure. By 2025, the network is the most dense and interconnected, indicating broader strategy mixing and more frequent transitions among understanding, implementation, debugging, and verification states.
cells.note: The study describes the transition-network shift qualitatively and prints no effect size.

O.outcome_detail: Weekly assignment scores and final course grades

result.effect: Assignment scores: Kruskal–Wallis H=3.23, p=0.357; assignment means 96.50 baseline, 96.28, 98.18, and 98.43; final-grade means 4.17, 4.28, 4.04, and 4.30

cells.quote: As shown in Table 2, assignment scores were consistently high and tightly clustered across cohorts. A Kruskal–Wallis test found no statistically significant differences across cohorts (H= 3.23,p= 0.357). Final-grade means were also broadly similar across years, suggesting that overall performance levels did not shift dramatically despite substantial changes in GenAI adoption and interaction patterns.
cells.note: The non-significant result is coded ns because no equivalence test or adequate-power claim is reported.
